text:
Predicates:
GivenOut(x, y) ::: Roses are given out on TV show x at time y.
On(x, y) ::: x is on TV show y.
Bachelor(x) ::: x is on the Bachelor.
Portrays(x, y) ::: x portrays the lives of real people on TV show y.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
Premises:
∃x (On(x, Monday8pm) ∧ GivenOut(x, Monday8pm)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x (GivenOut(x, bachelor) → Bachelor(x)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (On(x, bachelor) → Portrays(x, realPeople)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (Portrays(x, realPeople) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(breakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
GivenOut(breakingBad, Monday8pm) ::: Breaking Bad is a TV show in which roses are given out on Monday at 8 pm.
